clue.text: Prince gets a German beer mug for physicist

parts.note: Albert was the name of Queen Victoria's consort, Prince Albert
ein is the German word for 'a'
a stein is a large German beer mug

explanation.surface: A royal is handed a tankard of German beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two lights: ALBERT at 1 and EINSTEIN at 4.
explanation.definitionFit: The relativity theorist was the most famous scientist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: A number go to clergyman -that's right

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A count is assigned to a vicar's helper, and that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and exact are synonyms here: a right sum is a precise one.

clue.text: Programme for outspoken players

parts.note: broad humour is blunt and outspoken
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A show staged for actors who speak their minds.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio or television show is a transmission sent out to listeners.

clue.text: The others get a break

definitions.meaning: the remainder, everyone not yet mentioned
a pause or time off from work

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the remaining people and a pause for recovery.

clue.text: See 1
More than one Pope is blameless

definitions.meaning: thirteen popes have taken the papal name ...

explanation.definitionFit: Several pontiffs bore this name, and the word also means guiltless.

clue.text: People supporting speculator show inertness

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath, so the people come below the speculator

parts.note: a stag buys new share issues to sell quickly for profit
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A crowd backing a market gambler shows a lack of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts NATION under STAG in this down entry. STAG is Stock Exchange slang for a speculator in new issues.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of no movement or activity, like still water.

clue.text: Chaps go in to editor to make corrections

indicators.note: the chaps enter the editor, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Some men visit the editor's office to fix mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to revise it and remove its errors.

clue.text: Little boy on river has character

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it

parts.note: Nat is a short form of the boy's name Nathan or Nathaniel
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A small lad by the water has a strong personality.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's nature is their essential temperament or disposition.

clue.text: Customary drink

definitions.meaning: a regular's ... order at the bar, 'the ...'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means habitual, and a pub regular asks for 'the usual' as their regular tipple.

clue.text: Poor, so curse a wealthy man

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The poor curse the rich man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like the opposite of the definition but it signals the anagram of SO CURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The last king of Lydia was proverbial for great riches.

clue.text: Eastern assembly could not be closer

indicators.note: assembly means putting parts together, here the letters of the word given are put together afresh

explanation.surface: An Eastern parliament that could not be any nearer.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of near describes what is at the smallest distance.

clue.text: Swimmer, are you talking to theologian?

indicators.note: talking means the words are spoken, so their sound gives the letters

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like the letters R and U
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A swimmer asks whether you are talking to a scholar of religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' turns 'are you' into the letters RU, as in text speak.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Cultivating a garden cos, he shows off

indicators.note: cultivating ground turns it over, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A man growing lettuce in his garden boasts about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cos is a lettuce, here just fodder for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasconader is a braggart, named after the boastful reputation of Gascons.

clue.text: Police raid ordered to find magazine

indicators.note: ordered here means put into order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Officers are told to raid a place to find a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodical is a journal issued at regular intervals.

clue.text: Mistakenly eats the Spanish plant

indicators.note: done mistakenly means done wrongly, so these letters are set in a wrong order

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A Spaniard eats a plant by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a prickly plant whose heads were used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Establish fashionable stable

parts.note: in means in fashion
a stall is a compartment for one horse in a stable

explanation.surface: Set up a trendy stable.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something up or put it in place firmly is to establish it.

clue.text: Girl getting one duet arranged displays weariness

parts.note: lass is a girl
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: an arranged piece of music is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl with a duet arrangement to sing looks tired out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental tiredness and lack of energy.

clue.text: Strap grass up for caribou

parts.note: a rein is a strap for guiding a horse

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: Tie up some grass to feed the caribou.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer.

clue.text: Way to go on horseback not disheartened by grating

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ride is to travel on a horse

indicators.note: losing its heart leaves only the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A rider's way is to stay brave despite an irritating noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle letter of 'not', leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, rasping sound is strident.

clue.text: Footballer not working?

definitions.meaning: someone on strike is refusing to work

explanation.definitionFit: A goalscoring forward and someone downing tools in a dispute share this name.

clue.text: Some say Landor settled in this county

indicators.note: in tells us the answer is hidden inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rumour that the poet Walter Savage Landor made his home in this county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some say' only sets the rumour scene. DORSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county in south-west England.

clue.text: Cancels second game of dice

parts.note: craps is an American dice game

explanation.surface: A second round of dice is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap a plan is to abandon or cancel it.

clue.text: Sample delicacy

definitions.meaning: to try a little of something

explanation.definitionFit: One may try a morsel of food, and good judgment in style is also called this.

clue.text: Scottish lad once in a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A Scot who was once caught up in a catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland.

clue.text: Extremely lonely abstainer with a mass of cartilage

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, one who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A very lonely non-drinker has a lump of gristle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'lonely', L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A lytta is a rod of cartilage in the tongue of a dog or other carnivore.

clue.text: Im returning with little girl to the South of France

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are going back with a young girl to the French south.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Midi is the French name for southern France.

clue.text: Yearn for devout direction

parts.note: pi is a short form of pious, devout
NE is north-east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Long for a sense of religious guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to long for it.

clue.text: Recital could make newspaper feature

indicators.note: the letters of the word given could make something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A concert might give a reporter material for a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a written piece in a newspaper.

clue.text: Platform for magistrate

definitions.meaning: an official elected by the plebs in ancient Rome

explanation.definitionFit: A raised dais in a basilica and a Roman people's officer share this name.

clue.text: Alms collected by many to cook for unimportant people

indicators.note: collected means gathered and rearranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a large number
to fry is to cook in fat

explanation.surface: Charity gathered by a crowd is spent on feeding the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' rearranges ALMS into SMAL; L for 'many' completes the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Young fish are fry, and the phrase means people of no importance.

clue.text: Becoming modest

definitions.meaning: respectable, proper in dress or conduct

explanation.definitionFit: The word means suitable and also respectable in behaviour.
